title: Routing number and account number for direct deposit or ACH
summary: Our routing number is {{routingNumber}}. The member's full account number is shown in {{onlineBankingName}} and {{appName}} under Account Details.
steps: Log in to {{onlineBankingName}} or {{appName}}.
Select the checking or savings account you want deposits to go to.
Choose “Account Details” to see the full account number (tap the eye icon to reveal it).
Give your employer the routing number {{routingNumber}} and that account number. You can also download a pre-filled direct deposit form from the same screen.
repNotes: Never send a member's full account number over chat or email. Point them to Account Details or the pre-filled direct deposit form instead.

title: Reset a forgotten Online Banking password or username
summary: Members can reset their password themselves with the “Forgot password?” link on the {{onlineBankingName}} or {{appName}} login screen. After five failed attempts the account locks for 30 minutes.
steps: Go to the login screen on {{website}} or in {{appName}}.
Select “Forgot username or password?”.
Enter the requested identity details and the one-time code we text or email to the contact info on file.
Create a new password (at least 10 characters, with a number and a symbol).
repNotes: Never ask for or accept a member's password. If the phone or email on file is out of date, the member must verify identity by phone at {{phone}} or visit a branch.

title: Lost or stolen debit or credit card
summary: Members can lock their card instantly in {{appName}} under Card Controls. To cancel and replace it, call {{fraudPhone}} (available 24/7). A replacement arrives in {{policy.cardReplacementDays}}; rush delivery is available for {{policy.rushCardFee}}.
steps: Lock the card right away: {{appName}} → Cards → Card Controls → Lock card.
Review recent transactions for anything unfamiliar.
Call our 24/7 card line at {{fraudPhone}} to cancel the card and order a replacement.
Update any automatic payments with the new card number once it arrives.
repNotes: If the member reports unauthorized transactions, open a dispute (see Disputes) and flag for the fraud team.

title: Dispute an unauthorized or incorrect transaction
summary: Members can dispute a transaction within {{policy.disputeWindow}}. Disputes can be started in {{onlineBankingName}} by selecting the transaction and choosing “Dispute this transaction,” or by calling {{phone}}.
steps: Open the transaction in {{onlineBankingName}} or {{appName}}.
Select “Dispute this transaction” and tell us what happened.
If the card may be compromised, lock it in Card Controls and call {{fraudPhone}}.
We'll confirm receipt and keep you updated. Provisional credit may be issued while we investigate.
repNotes: For a card that may be compromised, escalate to the fraud team and do not promise a provisional credit amount or timeline beyond what the dispute policy states.

title: Mobile check deposit limits and availability
summary: Members can deposit checks in {{appName}} up to {{policy.mobileDepositDailyLimit}} per day. {{policy.mobileDepositHoldNote}}.
steps: Endorse the back of the check with your signature and “For Mobile Deposit Only at {{shortName}}.”
In {{appName}}, choose Deposit → Deposit a Check.
Photograph the front and back on a dark, flat surface in good light.
Keep the paper check for 30 days, then shred it.
repNotes: Rejected deposits are most often caused by missing endorsement wording or blurry images.

title: Overdraft protection and NSF fees
summary: Overdraft Transfer moves money from a linked savings account to cover a shortfall for a {{policy.overdraftTransferFee}} transfer fee. Items returned unpaid may incur a {{policy.nsfFee}} NSF fee.
steps: Link a savings account to checking in {{onlineBankingName}} → Account Services → Overdraft Protection.
Turn on low-balance alerts under Alerts so you're notified before an overdraft happens.
repNotes: Reps may not promise a fee refund over chat or email. Fee reversal requests go to a supervisor through the Fee Review queue.

title: Member asks for a fee to be refunded
summary: Fee reversal requests are reviewed by a supervisor. The rep can submit the request and let the member know they'll hear back within two business days.
steps: Confirm the fee type, date and amount with the member (no card or account numbers needed).
Submit the request in the Fee Review queue with a short note on the circumstances.
Let the member know a supervisor will review it and follow up within two business days.
repNotes: Don't promise an outcome. Acknowledge the member's frustration and set a clear follow-up expectation.
memberSummary: I've submitted a request for a supervisor to review the fee. You'll hear back from us within two business days.

title: Send a domestic wire transfer
summary: Domestic wires cost {{policy.wireDomesticFee}} and must be requested by {{policy.wireCutoff}} on a business day to go out the same day. For security, wires are initiated by phone at {{phone}} or in a branch, never by email.
steps: Have the recipient's name, bank name, routing number and account number ready.
Call {{phone}} or visit a branch to request the wire. We'll verify your identity before sending.
Before sending a wire for a home closing, confirm the instructions by calling the title company at a number you already know is real.
repNotes: Wire instructions received by email are a common fraud tactic. Never initiate a wire from an email or chat request.

title: When will my direct deposit post?
summary: {{policy.achPostingNote}}. Deposits post as soon as we receive them from the sender.
steps: Check the Pending section of the account in {{appName}}.
If the deposit hasn't arrived by the end of the scheduled payday, confirm with the employer or payer that it was sent to routing number {{routingNumber}} and the correct account.
repNotes: We can't see a deposit until the sending institution transmits it.

title: Branch and contact center hours
summary: Branches are open {{hours.branches}}. The contact center is available {{hours.contactCenter}} at {{phone}}. The 24/7 card line is {{fraudPhone}}.
steps: Find the nearest branch and today's hours with the Locations tool on {{website}} or in {{appName}}.

title: Surcharge-free ATMs and ATM limits
summary: Members can use {{policy.surchargeFreeAtms}} surcharge-free ATMs in the {{policy.atmNetwork}} networks. The daily ATM withdrawal limit is {{policy.atmDailyLimit}}.
steps: Use the ATM locator in {{appName}} (Locations → ATMs) to find surcharge-free ATMs nearby.
Call {{phone}} if you need a temporary limit increase.

title: Traveling with a debit or credit card
summary: Members can set a travel notice in {{appName}} under Cards → Travel Plans so their card keeps working while away.
steps: Open {{appName}} → Cards → Travel Plans.
Add your destinations and travel dates.
Make sure your mobile number is current so we can text you if we see unusual activity.
Save {{fraudPhone}} in your phone in case you need help while you're away.

title: Debit card declined
summary: Common causes are a locked card, insufficient available balance, the {{policy.debitPosDailyLimit}} daily purchase limit, or a fraud-prevention hold. Members can check Card Controls in {{appName}}.
steps: Check that the card isn't locked: {{appName}} → Cards → Card Controls.
Confirm the available balance (pending transactions reduce it).
If you received a fraud alert text, reply to confirm the purchase was yours.
If it still isn't working, call {{fraudPhone}} so we can look at the decline reason.

title: Who can join and how to open a membership
summary: Anyone who lives, works, worships or attends school in our service area, plus family members of current members, can join. Membership opens with a {{policy.membershipMinimum}}.
steps: Apply online at {{website}}/join (about 10 minutes) or visit any branch.
Have a government-issued photo ID and your Social Security number ready. You'll enter these in the secure application, not by email or chat.
Fund your Membership Savings account to complete membership.

title: Auto loan applications and rates
summary: Members can apply for new, used or refinance auto loans at {{website}}/loans or in {{appName}}. Current rates are listed on the Rates page and depend on credit history and term. Most decisions are made within one business day.
steps: Check current rates at {{website}}/rates.
Apply online or in {{appName}} → Apply → Auto Loan.
Pre-approval lets you shop with a set budget. It's typically valid for 60 days.
repNotes: Do not quote a specific rate in writing. Always direct members to the Rates page, because rates change and depend on credit.

title: Mortgages and home equity lines of credit
summary: Our mortgage team helps with purchases, refinances and home equity lines of credit. Members can apply at {{website}}/home or schedule a call with a mortgage loan officer.
steps: Review current rates at {{website}}/rates.
Schedule a no-obligation call with a mortgage loan officer at {{website}}/home.
Have recent pay stubs, two years of W-2s, and bank statements ready for the application.
repNotes: Refer detailed rate and qualification questions to a licensed mortgage loan officer.

title: Update address, phone number or email
summary: Members can update their address, phone and email in {{onlineBankingName}} under Profile & Settings. Name changes require a branch visit with legal documentation.
steps: Log in to {{onlineBankingName}} → Profile & Settings → Contact Information.
Update the details and confirm with the one-time code we send.
For a legal name change, bring a photo ID and the supporting document (such as a marriage certificate) to any branch.
repNotes: Contact info changes requested only through email or chat can't be completed by a rep. The member must make them in Online Banking or verify identity by phone.

title: Access statements and tax forms
summary: Statements are issued {{policy.statementCycle}} and are available for 7 years in {{onlineBankingName}} under Documents. Tax forms (1099-INT, 1098) are posted by January 31.
steps: Log in to {{onlineBankingName}} → Documents → Statements (or Tax Forms).
Select the month or year and download the PDF.

title: Sending money to friends and family (person-to-person payments)
summary: Members can send money to people they know and trust from {{appName}} under Transfers → Pay a Person, using the recipient's phone number or email.
steps: Open {{appName}} → Transfers → Pay a Person.
Enter the recipient's mobile number or email and the amount.
Double-check the recipient before sending. These payments usually can't be reversed.
repNotes: If a member says they were pressured to send money by someone claiming to be from the credit union, a utility or a government agency, treat it as a possible scam and escalate.

title: Suspicious call, text or email claiming to be the credit union
summary: {{shortName}} will never call, text or email to ask for a password, PIN, full card number or one-time verification code. If a member shared any of these, they should call {{fraudPhone}} right away.
steps: Don't reply to the message or call back the number it came from.
If you shared a code, password or card number, call {{fraudPhone}} immediately so we can secure your account.
Change your {{onlineBankingName}} password.
Forward suspicious emails to our security team and then delete them.
repNotes: Treat any shared credentials as urgent. Escalate to the fraud team immediately.

title: Close an account or membership
summary: Accounts can be closed in a branch or by signed written request. Before closing, members should move automatic payments and direct deposits and wait for outstanding checks to clear.
steps: Move direct deposits and automatic payments to the new account.
Make sure all outstanding checks and pending transactions have cleared.
Visit a branch or call {{phone}} to complete the closure. We'll send the remaining balance by check or transfer.
repNotes: Ask (politely, once) if there's anything we could do better and log retention feedback.

title: Reporting the death of a member
summary: We're sorry for the loss. Our Estate Services team will guide the family through next steps. They'll need a certified death certificate and, if applicable, letters of administration or testamentary.
steps: Call {{phone}} and ask for Estate Services, or visit any branch.
Bring a certified copy of the death certificate and your photo ID.
If you are the executor, bring the court-issued letters testamentary or letters of administration.
repNotes: Lead with condolences. Do not discuss account details until the requester's authority is verified. Escalate to Estate Services.

title: Add a beneficiary (payable on death) or joint owner
summary: Members can add a payable-on-death beneficiary in {{onlineBankingName}} under Account Services. Adding a joint owner requires both people to sign in a branch.
steps: For a beneficiary: {{onlineBankingName}} → Account Services → Beneficiaries, then enter their name, relationship and date of birth.
For a joint owner: schedule a branch visit. Both people should bring photo ID.

title: Member wants to file a complaint
summary: We take every complaint seriously. The rep should acknowledge the concern, apologize for the experience, capture the details, and route the complaint to a supervisor, who follows up within two business days.
steps: Thank the member for telling us and apologize for the experience.
Capture what happened, when, and what outcome the member is hoping for.
Log the complaint in the Complaint Tracker and route it to a supervisor.
Tell the member who will follow up and when.
repNotes: Complaints are a regulatory record. Always log them, even when resolved on the spot.
memberSummary: Thank you for telling us about this. I'm sorry for the experience. I've documented what happened and shared it with a supervisor, who will follow up with you within two business days.
